questions.question_english:
70. Consider the following statements regarding the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India:
A. The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the constitutional provisions for GST.
B. GST is an origin-based tax levied at the point of manufacture rather than consumption.
C. Alcohol for human consumption and specified petroleum products were kept outside the immediate purview of GST.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 enabled the statutory rollout of the Goods and Services Tax in India. Items like alcoholic liquor for human consumption and specified petroleum crude products remain excluded from GST. However, GST is structurally a destination-based consumption tax levied at the final point of consumption, rather than an origin-based indirect tax levied at the point of initial manufacture.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। 101वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2016 ने भारत में वस्तु एवं सेवा कर के वैधानिक कार्यान्वयन को सक्षम किया। मानव उपभोग के लिए शराब और निर्दिष्ट पेट्रोलियम कच्चे उत्पाद GST से बाहर रखे गए हैं। हालाँकि, GST संरचनात्मक रूप से एक गंतव्य-आधारित उपभोग कर है जो अंतिम उपभोग के बिंदु पर लगाया जाता है, न कि प्रारंभिक निर्माण के बिंदु पर लगाया जाने वाला उत्पत्ति-आधारित अप्रत्यक्ष कर।
questions.topic: Basic Economic Concepts and Structure of the Indian Economy
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) A and C only

questions.question_english: 51. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at Market Prices is derived from Gross Value Added (GVA) at Basic Prices by adding:
options_english: Product Subsidies and subtracting Product Taxes
Factor Cost and subtracting Indirect Taxes
Product Taxes and subtracting Product Subsidies
Depreciation and subtracting Consumption of Fixed Capital
questions.explanation_english: To derive Gross Domestic Product at market prices from Gross Value Added at basic prices, net product taxes must be incorporated by adding all product taxes paid and subtracting all product subsidies received on final output. questions.question_english: 2. How do you convert market prices to factor costs in economic measurements?
options_english: Subtract Indirect Taxes and add Subsidies
questions.explanation_english: Net Domestic Product at market prices measures output using actual prevailing transactional prices, which inherently reflect market distortions like government taxes and financial support. Factor cost reflects the true earning cost of productive resources utilized in production. Converting market price estimates to factor cost requires removing indirect taxes because they artificially inflate market prices, while adding back government subsidies since they lower market prices below true factor costs.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। बाजार मूल्य पर शुद्ध घरेलू उत्पाद (NDP) वास्तविक प्रचलित लेनदेन मूल्य का उपयोग करके उत्पादन को मापता है, जो स्वाभाविक रूप से सरकारी करों और वित्तीय सहायता जैसी बाजार विकृतियों को दर्शाता है। कारक लागत उत्पादन में उपयोग किए गए उत्पादक संसाधनों की वास्तविक कमाई लागत को दर्शाती है। बाजार मूल्य के अनुमान को कारक लागत में परिवर्तित करने के लिए अप्रत्यक्ष करों को हटाना आवश्यक है क्योंकि ये बाजार मूल्यों को कृत्रिम रूप से बढ़ाते हैं, जबकि सरकारी सब्सिडी को जोड़ना आवश्यक है क्योंकि ये बाजार मूल्यों को वास्तविक कारक लागत से नीचे लाते हैं।
